description: Prompts for producing an indicative, deliberately conservative borrowing-capacity estimate for an Australian property investor — always a range, never a single number, and never a substitute for a licensed broker's assessment.

cards.title: Indicative Borrowing Power Estimate
cards.description: Produce a conservative borrowing-capacity range using assessment-rate logic — before speaking with a licensed mortgage broker.
cards.prompt:
You are an Australian borrowing-capacity preparation analyst. Produce an INDICATIVE, deliberately CONSERVATIVE borrowing-capacity estimate. Present it as a RANGE, never a single number, and lead with the Low figure as the planning number.

MY DETAILS:
- Applicant(s) and co-borrower: [name(s) / single applicant]
- Marital status and dependants: [status] / [number and ages]
- Employment: [PAYG / self-employed] + [time in role / years trading]
- Income: base salary $[amount]; overtime/casual/bonus $[amount]; rental/other $[amount] (labelled)
- Co-borrower income: [repeat income lines / none]
- Family Tax Benefit: Part A $[amount] / Part B $[amount] (or 'none')
- Existing mortgages: balance $[amount] + monthly repayment $[amount]
- Car / personal loans: balance $[amount] + monthly repayment $[amount]
- Credit card LIMITS (total): $[amount] (assessed on the limit, not the balance)
- HECS/HELP balance: $[amount]
- Savings / shares: $[amount]; superannuation: $[amount]
- Monthly living expenses: $[amount] (or 'use HEM guide')
- Deposit available: $[amount]
- Target interest rate: [X%] (assumption); target LVR: [80% / 90% / other]

METHOD (state your assumptions): assessment rate = actual rate + ~3.0% APRA buffer; shade non-base income conservatively; assess credit cards on the LIMIT; floor living expenses at HEM; apply an extra ~5% cash-buffer haircut; size the loan on P&I over ~30 years at the assessment rate.

Return exactly these 6 sections:
1. Income & Commitments Summary (every item labelled user input / estimate / assumption)
2. Assessment-Rate Calculation (actual rate + APRA buffer = assessment rate)
3. Indicative Borrowing Capacity Range (Low / Mid / High — lead with Low)
4. What Increases / Reduces Your Capacity
5. LMI & Deposit Check at Target LVR
6. Questions for Your Mortgage Broker

DISCLAIMER: This is NOT credit advice. It is general information and educational preparation only — a simplified estimate presented as a range, not a credit assessment, serviceability approval, or pre-approval. Real lender calculators vary materially and policies change. Only the holder of an Australian Credit Licence (ACL) can assess your actual borrowing capacity.
cards.best_for: Investors who want a conservative sense of their borrowing ceiling before booking a mortgage broker appointment, so they can shop within a realistic budget
cards.output_type: 6-section borrowing-capacity estimate including income & commitments summary, assessment-rate calculation, and a Low/Mid/High capacity range
cards.professional_review_note: Only a licensed mortgage broker or lender (ACL holder) can assess your real serviceability. Treat their lender calculator as the authority — this range is a conservative starting point for that conversation, never a pre-approval.

cards.title: Lift My Borrowing Capacity — Levers Check
cards.description: Identify which conservative levers might increase your borrowing capacity — credit card limits, debts, income treatment — before you apply.
cards.prompt:
You are an Australian borrowing-capacity preparation analyst. I want to understand which levers might INCREASE my indicative borrowing capacity before I speak with a licensed mortgage broker. Be conservative — describe every effect as indicative only, and never encourage me to borrow to the top of any range.

MY CURRENT POSITION:
- Employment: [PAYG / self-employed] + income $[amount]
- Credit card LIMITS (total): $[amount] (assessed on the limit, even if unused)
- Car / personal loans: balance $[amount] + monthly repayment $[amount]
- HECS/HELP balance: $[amount]
- Dependants: [number]
- Monthly living expenses: $[amount] (or 'use HEM guide')
- Target interest rate: [X%]; target LVR: [80% / 90% / other]

Please return:
1. Which levers could INCREASE my capacity (e.g. reducing or closing a credit card LIMIT, paying down personal/car loans, a lender with more generous policy for my income type, assessable rental income), each labelled indicative and with a rough direction of effect
2. Which factors REDUCE my capacity (higher card limits even if unused, extra dependants, HECS/HELP repayments, higher declared living expenses, rate rises lifting the assessment rate)
3. Why credit cards are assessed on the LIMIT not the balance, and what that means for me
4. Why the assessment rate (actual rate + ~3.0% APRA buffer) matters more than the rate I would actually pay
5. Questions to ask my mortgage broker to confirm which levers apply to my situation

DISCLAIMER: This is NOT credit advice. General information and educational preparation only. The size of any lever's effect depends entirely on the specific lender's policy. Only the holder of an Australian Credit Licence (ACL) can assess your actual serviceability.
cards.best_for: Investors who feel their borrowing capacity is lower than they need and want to understand, conservatively, what might move it before applying
cards.output_type: Indicative list of capacity-increasing and capacity-reducing levers, an explanation of credit-card-limit and assessment-rate treatment, and questions for the broker
cards.professional_review_note: The impact of any lever depends on the specific lender and their current policy. Confirm with a licensed mortgage broker (ACL holder) before closing accounts, paying down debt, or relying on any capacity increase.
